{"artifact":"SmeDossierEnvelope","schema_version":"0.4.0","stage_id":"02.dossier_sections","probe":"rdmv-mn-d","lineage":{"input_manifest_sha256":"fcf81115ca5930044dc2ae9eaa87acd60f4a54e9982d6956504eafe8aa22a627","candidate_lineage_id":"2026-10-28-rdmv-mn-class-d:lineage:51","source_registry_sha256":"960e2daa314aff60b32f5124e42324d79615ce2a3ea953a336216b4593c0c910","source_liveness_sha256":"0b70283fc58b1f8ea1822994a92e3ce7ff4b722004376a9cd819180969b6fe1e"},"envelope_scope":{"kind":"partial_chunk","assigned_section_ids":["C2"],"chunk_index":1,"chunk_total":1},"section_char_limit":12000,"sections":[{"section_id":"C2","chunk_id":"C2.01","merge_seq":1,"domain":"Driving conditions part two confusables and continuation facts","heading":"C2 — Confusable pairs and continuation facts: towing handling and length limits, winter parking and plows, staying awake, hills and narrow roads, brake and steering failures, submersion, wiper, hood and headlight failures, and carbon monoxide habits","learner_facing":false,"markdown":"## C2 — Confusable pairs and continuation facts: towing handling and length limits, winter parking and plows, staying awake, hills and narrow roads, brake and steering failures, submersion, wiper, hood and headlight failures, and carbon monoxide habits
Confusable pairs from the second half of the driving conditions chapter, followed by continuation facts; each block ties to one manual page, and hint metadata sits only in the trailing line of a block.

FACT_ID: sec12-R01 | anchor: A01
Recreational trailers must show a clearly visible plate with current registration, and every trailer needs a safety chain that stays permanently fixed to it and is hooked to the towing vehicle. [A01]
Why it matters: group trailers; difficulty low.
Source: [A01 -> pdf-0083]

FACT_ID: sec12-R02 | anchor: A01
Wind and rain make a heavy towing load harder to control, so slow down even more than usual in wet or windy weather when pulling a trailer or camper. [A01]
Why it matters: group towing; difficulty low.
Source: [A01 -> pdf-0083]

FACT_ID: sec12-R03 | anchor: A01
Leave plenty of room when turning with a long trailer, because it swings closer to the road edge than your vehicle does, and watch the cooling system, which overheats more easily in heat, at speed and on hills. [A01]
Why it matters: group towing; difficulty medium.
Source: [A01 -> pdf-0083]

FACT_ID: sec12-R04 | anchor: A01
Type A, B or C motor homes may be up to 45 feet long, the same as a trailer, while the general limit for single-unit vehicles is 40 feet and a recreational vehicle combination may reach 70 feet. [A01]
Why it matters: group length limits; confusable forty-five versus forty versus seventy; difficulty high.
Source: [A01 -> pdf-0083]

FACT_ID: sec12-R05 | anchor: A01
The 102-inch width limit for recreational vehicles excludes attachments that stay within the exterior rearview mirrors on a self-propelled recreational vehicle. [A01]
Why it matters: group width limits; difficulty high.
Source: [A01 -> pdf-0083]

FACT_ID: sec12-R06 | anchor: A01
A recreational vehicle combination's trailer may carry items such as watercraft, motorcycles, snowmobiles, all-terrain vehicles, golf carts or equestrian equipment. [A01]
Why it matters: group recreational vehicle combinations; difficulty low.
Source: [A01 -> pdf-0083]

FACT_ID: sec12-R07 | anchor: A02
After heavy snow, city officials may declare a snow emergency with special parking rules, and obeying them avoids towing and fines. [A02]
Why it matters: group winter parking; difficulty low.
Source: [A02 -> pdf-0084]

FACT_ID: sec12-R08 | anchor: A02
Snowplows can raise clouds of blowing snow that hide the road, move slowly, and may back up to turn around in residential areas, so give operators room. [A02]
Why it matters: group snowplows; difficulty medium.
Source: [A02 -> pdf-0084]

FACT_ID: sec12-R09 | anchor: A02
If the tires start to spin or slide while you rock a stuck vehicle, apply the brake and repeat the move in the opposite direction. [A02]
Why it matters: group stuck vehicle; difficulty medium.
Source: [A02 -> pdf-0084]

FACT_ID: sec12-R10 | anchor: A03
While stranded, turn on hazard lights, tie a red flag to the antenna or door handle, set out flags and flares if you can, and bring any supplies from the trunk inside. [A03]
Why it matters: group winter survival; difficulty low.
Source: [A03 -> pdf-0085]

FACT_ID: sec12-R11 | anchor: A03
At least one person in a stranded vehicle should stay awake at all times. [A03]
Why it matters: group winter survival; difficulty low.
Source: [A03 -> pdf-0085]

FACT_ID: sec12-R12 | anchor: A03
Alertness tips such as talking with passengers, singing, the radio or fresh air do not last, so do not rely on stay-awake drugs; let someone else drive, or stop for the day or park well off the road with doors locked and windows slightly open. [A03]
Why it matters: group fatigue; difficulty medium.
Source: [A03 -> pdf-0085]

FACT_ID: sec12-R13 | anchor: A03
The stranded-vehicle rule is ten minutes of engine time each hour, while the fatigue rule is a stop at least every 100 miles or every two hours. [A03]
Why it matters: group winter and fatigue; confusable engine time versus rest stops; difficulty medium.
Source: [A03 -> pdf-0085]

FACT_ID: sec12-R14 | anchor: A04
At 35 mph or less most tires wipe water away and keep contact with the road, while at higher speeds water can collect under the tires and lift them off the surface. [A04]
Why it matters: group hydroplaning; difficulty high.
Source: [A04 -> pdf-0086]

FACT_ID: sec12-R15 | anchor: A04
Good tires with deep treads make hydroplaning less likely at normal highway speeds because they let water escape. [A04]
Why it matters: group hydroplaning; difficulty medium.
Source: [A04 -> pdf-0086]

FACT_ID: sec12-R16 | anchor: A04
On narrow roads with curves or brush and trees blocking the view, you may sound the horn to warn others that you are coming. [A04]
Why it matters: group narrow roads; difficulty low.
Source: [A04 -> pdf-0086]

FACT_ID: sec12-R17 | anchor: A04
Do not coast down steep hills in neutral, and check the speedometer often, because speed builds even with your foot off the accelerator. [A04]
Why it matters: group hills; difficulty low.
Source: [A04 -> pdf-0086]

FACT_ID: sec12-R18 | anchor: A04
Warning signs of a blowout include a thumping sound or the steering wheel pulling to one side. [A04]
Why it matters: group blowouts; difficulty low.
Source: [A04 -> pdf-0086]

FACT_ID: sec12-R19 | anchor: A05
A brake pedal that sinks slowly under pressure warns that the brakes may be failing, and a warning light should come on for a serious problem. [A05]
Why it matters: group brake failure; confusable slow sink versus sudden drop; difficulty medium.
Source: [A05 -> pdf-0087]

FACT_ID: sec12-R20 | anchor: A05
If road conditions let you coast, shift into a lower gear and keep downshifting as you slow until you can pull over safely. [A05]
Why it matters: group brake failure; difficulty medium.
Source: [A05 -> pdf-0087]

FACT_ID: sec12-R21 | anchor: A05
With steering failure the vehicle may keep a straight line on its own as you slow down. [A05]
Why it matters: group steering failure; difficulty low.
Source: [A05 -> pdf-0087]

FACT_ID: sec12-R22 | anchor: A05
Deer usually cross in rural areas but can wander into towns or cities, and they may cross anywhere at any time. [A05]
Why it matters: group deer; difficulty low.
Source: [A05 -> pdf-0087]

FACT_ID: sec12-R23 | anchor: A05
Never move into the left lane to avoid a vehicle coming at you in your lane, because that driver may swerve back into their own lane and into your path. [A05]
Why it matters: group oncoming threats; difficulty medium.
Source: [A05 -> pdf-0087]

FACT_ID: sec12-R24 | anchor: A05
If a crash with a failed passer seems likely and the right shoulder is wide enough, move quickly onto it so the passing vehicle can take your lane. [A05]
Why it matters: group passing threats; difficulty medium.
Source: [A05 -> pdf-0087]

FACT_ID: sec12-R25 | anchor: A06
Flash floods can arrive within minutes or hours of heavy rain, and floodwater can hide dips or washed-out pavement even when it looks shallow, so be extra careful at night. [A06]
Why it matters: group floods; difficulty medium.
Source: [A06 -> pdf-0088]

FACT_ID: sec12-R26 | anchor: A06
Doors of a submerged vehicle will not open until the water pressure inside equals the pressure outside, the heavy engine makes the front sink first, and the rear seats may hold an air pocket. [A06]
Why it matters: group submersion; difficulty high.
Source: [A06 -> pdf-0088]

FACT_ID: sec12-R27 | anchor: A06
If others are in a submerged vehicle, check on them and try to get out together. [A06]
Why it matters: group submersion; difficulty low.
Source: [A06 -> pdf-0088]

FACT_ID: sec12-R28 | anchor: A06
Stop-and-go traffic on a hot day, steep climbs and towing can make an engine run hotter than normal. [A06]
Why it matters: group overheating; difficulty low.
Source: [A06 -> pdf-0088]

FACT_ID: sec12-R29 | anchor: A07
If your headlights fail, try the parking lights, hazard lights or turn signals, and on a dark, empty road slow down and stay on the pavement until you can safely move to the shoulder. [A07]
Why it matters: group headlight failure; difficulty medium.
Source: [A07 -> pdf-0089]

FACT_ID: sec12-R30 | anchor: A07
If the wipers fail in heavy rain or snow, slow down, turn on the hazard lights, avoid sudden braking with traffic behind, and pull off as soon as you can. [A07]
Why it matters: group wiper failure; difficulty low.
Source: [A07 -> pdf-0089]

FACT_ID: sec12-R31 | anchor: A07
If the hood flies up and blocks your view, look through the gap under it or lean out the window to see past it, then use hazard lights, slow down and steer off the road. [A07]
Why it matters: group hood failure; difficulty medium.
Source: [A07 -> pdf-0089]

FACT_ID: sec12-R32 | anchor: A07
If a stuck gas pedal leaves you on an unpaved shoulder, turn on hazard lights and keep steering straight until you can pull over safely. [A07]
Why it matters: group stuck accelerator; difficulty medium.
Source: [A07 -> pdf-0089]

FACT_ID: sec12-R33 | anchor: A08
Also avoid driving with every window shut, keep the exhaust system free of leaks and blockages, and lower the windows now and then for fresh air. [A08]
Why it matters: group carbon monoxide; difficulty low.
Source: [A08 -> pdf-0090]
